messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Error in min(summarysleep$night):max(summarysleep$night)
parts:
Could you provide a reproducible example, meaning: data file + full R code?

Also notice that GGIR has parameter maxRecordingInterval that may offer a solution for the split recordings as it appends neighbouring short recordings with the same participant ID together into one longer recording.

Vincent

On Tuesday, 15 October 2024 at 4:04 AM, Emma Guyonnet <emmagu...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hello,

I'm analyzing NHANES data 2011-2014 (https://wwwn.cdc.gov/Nchs/Nhanes/2011-2012/PAX80_G.htm). I combined the csv files per participant into one file per participant and am now trying to run GGIR.

Since there are 10,000+ files to run, I wanted to test GGIR on one participant file first before running GGIR on all the files. Here is my code and the error:

Any tips on how to fix it would be great. Thank you so much!

> g.shell.GGIR(datadir="XXX", + outputdir="XXX", + studyname="TEST", + rmc.nrow = Inf, + rmc.skip = 0, + rmc.dec = ".", + rmc.firstrow.acc = 2, + rmc.col.acc = 2:4, + rmc.col.time=1, + rmc.unit.acc = "g", + desiredtz ="America/Chicago", + rmc.unit.time = "POSIX", + rmc.format.time = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%OS", + rmc.sf = 80, + overwrite = FALSE, + print.filename=TRUE, + minloadcrit = 72, + data_masking_strategy = 2, #only the data between the first midnight and the last midnight is used + ndayswindow=7, + maxdur = 9, + includedaycrit = 16, + includenightcrit = 16, + excludefirstlast = FALSE, #If TRUE then the first and last night of the measurement are ignored for the sleep assessment in g.part4. + ignorenonwear = TRUE, #If TRUE then ignore detected monitor non-wear periods to avoid confusion between monitor non-wear time and sustained inactivity. + qwindow=c(0,24), + def.noc.sleep = 1, + outliers.only = FALSE, + criterror = 1, + #------------------------------- + # Part 6 parameters: + #------------------------------- + part6CR = TRUE, + epochvalues2csv=TRUE) Part 1 Checking that user has read access permission for all files in data directory: Yes 1 File name: 62161_combined.csv ___________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________ Part 2 1 ___________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________ Part 3 1 ___________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________ Part 4 ___________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________ Part 5 1 Error in min(summarysleep$night):max(summarysleep$night) : NA/NaN argument In addition: Warning messages: 1: In min(summarysleep$night) : no non-missing arguments, returning NA 2: In max(summarysleep$night) : no non-missing arguments, returning NA
